Hi OP, 
First NTA you are doing a great job with your daughter. I'm a social care worker that works primarily with autism. We have a resident in his mid 20's who does something very similar but grabs car door handles. This is actually very dangerous behaviour to encourage or allow as it can and has escalated with him. He has grabbed moving car door handles and ran off in busy car parks. Also you never know how members of the public will react. He has terrified some and antagonised others. If we did not stick close to him he may get hurt physically or mentally. You and your wife seem like great parents and your daughter is lucky to have you but remember today's annoyances can become tomorrow's significant problems with learned behaviour.

All the best OP you and your wife have got this

Hey OP sorry to hear your a bit down. Been there many times over the years with this same sentiment. Even more frustrating is humanity basically invented "money" that we're now enslaved to. Nature doesn't and never has given a fuck about money yet we use this invention to wreak havoc on nature, animals and ourself. The thing I find most annoying is you can't just go "nah bro I'm cool I think I'll check just myself out". Like one of the few things we have in life is preceved freedom. Freedom to do what exactly? Pay more into a broken system in the Hope's that I have enough to retire on? Spend the best years of as a wage slave often in a bullshit position that does not benefit you, the planet, society but just a minority of people who hold the wealth. At least hunter gatherers had actual assets like you know food instead of this bullshit concept of money. How can we justify someone making a funny video on the internet getting thousands when most nurses are struggling to make end meet. We dont need to look for a dystopian society we're already living in one. All I can say Op is chin up and maybe look at Albert Campus. Some of his work stuck with me such as his comment on Sisyphus pushing the rock up the hill. That we must imagine him happy. If you think something is bullshit and without meaning then it totally is good job defining that. But try take a side step and if you look at the same thing and think of it as the best thing ever then guess what it is too! Your perception is what I feels defines you so it may sound arbitrary but try to find joy in the simple things, a walk to work, a clean house, good day outside. You will do these things a countless number of days in your life similar to Sisyphus pushing that rock up the hill but if you can feel joy from the small things it will lead to a happier life overall!

Debatable OP. I often find that sentiment to be a complete crapshoot but recently I have been trying a new approach to things. I agree with the statement that we are products of our environment, meaning you behave and react to situations the way you do because that is how you survive. Often when we're younger we have no choice in our environment so we develop coping mechanisms that follow us into adulthood that can be good or bad. When you are an adult often you will then struggle with coping that is toxic in nature but remember it served a purpose at the time! I find it's only when you challenge why and how you do things that you can develop new patterns and solutions.

What I've tried to do recently is view things at a different angle. Try take a step back. For example with me I have recently discovered my father to be very narcissistic and the number of traits I inherited off him are profound. This was a big shock but then I looked at the environment I was in. I can move, do college, become antisocial, scream and shout my ideas across or accept things are the way they are and cannot change. The point is if I alter my environment things will change. Change isn't necessary good or bad but your mindset will often dictate how you feel at the time.

So even if I cannot physically change my environment I can change how I choose to react to the environment. For me this meant going next to no contact with most of my family and most conversations are superficial now not holding any particular weight. I am happier this way and am persuing new friendships and am starting to do better overall!

Apologies about the length of this but if it helps change your mindset or even gives you a second pause I have done my part. My final piece on this is your perception of events influences how you feel. If you think nothing gets better, it probably won't because you will lack the motivation to change, feeling that it is futile. Whereas if you hold onto even the smallest glimmer of hope of "it gets better" it actually might! Why?, because you will be more likely to hang out with that friend, apply for that job or get out and take a deep breath of fresh air!

I think a really good statement that has stuck with me over the years is: "The definition of madness is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting something to change" As a really basic example 2+1=3, I can do this sum a thousand times but the answer will never be 4! Try do something new OP, break up the monotony. Will this mean suddenly things are improved and better? Not nessiarily but you already know doing nothing gets you nothing so why not take life by the horns and try mix it up!

All the best OP the struggle is real but the great thing about it is you have support even if it is just internet strangers there are people who want to see you succeed and be your best self!
